Site.name: Reform Monitor
Site.title: Reform Monitor: Chapters 23 and 24
Site.description: An independent demonstration monitor of measures under Chapter 23 “Judiciary and fundamental rights” and Chapter 24 “Justice, freedom and security”.
Site.disclaimer: Independent demonstration project. Not an official resource of the authorities of Ukraine or the EU.
Site.demoDataNote: Benchmark wording, measures, deadlines and statuses on this site are demonstration data. They illustrate how the platform works and do not reflect the actual state of reforms.

Home.title: Reforms for joining the EU: courts, human rights, security
Home.lead: To become a member of the European Union, Ukraine has to carry out reforms in many areas — in the accession talks they are called chapters. This site covers two of them: Chapter 23 (courts, anti-corruption, human rights) and Chapter 24 (borders, migration, fighting organised crime). For each measure you can see who is responsible, the deadline and what has been done so far.

Methodology.title: Methodology
Methodology.lead: How progress is calculated, where the data comes from and when it was last updated.
Methodology.structure: Data is organised in five levels: chapter → reform direction → interim benchmark → measure → status update. Each measure belongs to one benchmark and has a responsible body, a deadline and a status.
Methodology.formula: Progress is the share of completed measures. Each measure gets a weight depending on its status; the sum of weights is divided by the number of measures.
Methodology.weightsCaption: Status weights used in the progress calculation
Methodology.formulaText: Progress = (done + 0.5 × partially done) ÷ total number of measures × 100%
Methodology.levels: The same calculation applies to a direction, a chapter and all measures together. The result is rounded to a whole percent.
Methodology.overdue: The “Overdue” status is never entered manually: it is computed automatically when the deadline has passed and the measure is not “Done”. In the progress calculation such a measure counts by its actual status.
Methodology.sources: Data is entered by editors in the admin panel or imported from a Google Sheets spreadsheet. The import is idempotent: a repeated run updates existing records and creates no duplicates. Every status change is recorded in the measure’s history.

About.title: About the project
About.lead: An independent open project: an example monitoring platform built with Next.js, Payload CMS and PostgreSQL.
About.what: The Reform Monitor shows how implementation of measures under Chapters 23 and 24 of the “Fundamentals” negotiating cluster can be tracked: from chapter and direction down to an individual measure with its responsible body, deadline and status history.
features: Bilingual interface and content: Ukrainian and English.
Data-driven roles: a read / write / delete matrix for every collection.
A tamper-proof audit log: updates and deletions are blocked at database level.
Idempotent data import from Google Sheets with a run log.
WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility in our own code, with automated axe-core checks.
An open API with an OpenAPI 3.1 specification.
One-command deployment with Docker Compose, backups and documentation.
About.author: Vadym Nersesov — development and maintenance.
About.repo: The code is open under the MIT licence.
About.stack: Next.js (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Payload CMS 3, PostgreSQL 16, Docker Compose, Caddy.
